entries.originalText: Open not thine heart to every man, but deal with one who is wise and feareth God.
entries.modernizedText: Do not open your heart to everyone, but deal with someone who is wise and fears God.

entries.originalText: Be seldom with the young and with strangers.
entries.modernizedText: Spend little time with the young and with strangers.

entries.originalText: Be not a flatterer of the rich; nor willingly seek the society of the great.
entries.modernizedText: Do not flatter the rich or willingly seek the company of the great.

entries.originalText: Let thy company be the humble and the simple, the devout and the gentle, and let thy discourse be concerning things which edify.
entries.modernizedText: Let your company be the humble and the simple, the devout and the gentle, and let your conversation concern things that edify.

entries.originalText: Be not familiar with any woman, but commend all good women alike unto God.
entries.modernizedText: Do not be familiar with any woman, but commend all good women alike to God.

entries.originalText: Choose for thy companions God and His Angels only, and flee from the notice of men.
entries.modernizedText: Choose God and His Angels alone for your companions, and flee from the notice of others.

entries.originalText: We must love all men, but not make close companions of all.
entries.modernizedText: We must love everyone, but not make close companions of everyone.

entries.originalText: It sometimes falleth out that one who is unknown to us is highly regarded through good report of him, whose actual person is nevertheless unpleasing to those who behold it.
entries.modernizedText: It sometimes happens that someone unknown to us is highly regarded because of a good report, yet his actual person is displeasing to those who see him.

entries.originalText: We sometimes think to please others by our intimacy, and forthwith displease them the more by the faultiness of character which they perceive in us.
entries.modernizedText: We sometimes think to please others by our intimacy and immediately displease them all the more by the faults of character they perceive in us.
